core_obligations: Set up (proof lines 3511-3520): the pullback is the sheafification of the presheaf U maps to the colimit over morphisms U -> V with V an object of the source site of the values of F, so by the agreement lemma for affine weakly contractible objects it suffices to show that this presheaf sends finite disjoint unions to products.

Compute the colimit over a disjoint union (proof lines 3520-3534): for U = U_1 disjoint union U_2 there is a functor from the product of the categories of morphisms U_i -> V_i to the category of morphisms U -> V sending a pair to the disjoint union V_1 disjoint union V_2, and this functor is initial, so the induced functor on opposite categories is cofinal and the colimit over morphisms from U is the colimit of the values on the disjoint unions over the product category.

Conclude (proof lines 3534-3537): since F is a sheaf it sends disjoint unions to products, so the presheaf in question does too, and the agreement lemma applied to the affine weakly contractible W gives the displayed formula for the value of the pullback.
proof_roadmap: Recall the description of the pullback and reduce to a property of a presheaf.
Show that the presheaf of colimits sends finite disjoint unions to products by an initiality argument.
Apply the agreement of sheafification with the presheaf on affine weakly contractible objects.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a morphism f : X -> Y and a sheaf of sets F on the pro-etale site of Y, the value of the pullback at an affine weakly contractible object W of X is the colimit of the values of F over the morphisms W -> V over Y (statement lines 3499-3509). The proof (proof lines 3511-3538) identifies the pullback as the sheafification of a colimit presheaf, proves through an initiality argument that this presheaf sends finite disjoint unions to products, and concludes by the agreement lemma for affine weakly contractible objects. H2: two steps with three inputs, written out in full.
